what: The epic as a whole, before against after, under comparable conditions: interleaved runs (before, after, before, after) on the same machine within one hour. SwiftShader (the headless harness) and the hardware GPU (headed) are kept apart.

before.built: git archive 19e9fbf, wasm built from its own Rust (wasm-pack 0.13.1), its own @perf harness

after.built: the motion-005 Red-approved tree, wasm rebuilt with the same wasm-pack
after.note: the product code at 23da733 is identical to the motion-005 Gold commits (Gold changes docs, tests and CI only; the one product edit is a comment in App.tsx)

tickMsMean.source: @perf harness, baseline 1×: measured tick time per frame ÷ ticks (worker, wasm)

nativeStepMsMedian.source: cargo run -p sim-core --release --example frame_cost_probe -- baseline (native release, River City x1)
nativeStepMsMedian.note: each value is one run: the mean step time over 2000 ticks after 1 sim h; the median is taken across runs

frameBytes.definition: vehicle records (16 B each) + next links (2 B each), plus trip ids (4 B each) after the epic: the per-vehicle buffers of one frame; per-link arrays are not counted

transferBytesPerS.source: epic_probe.mjs, running at 20× for 10 s: the byteLength of every ArrayBuffer and typed array in the frame messages the UI received (vehicle records included); small plain fields are not counted

pausedFramesPerS.source: epic_probe.mjs, paused (after 2 s settling), 5 s window

1x.source: epic_probe.mjs: the Diagnostics presentation lag, median of 100 ms samples over 10 s at 1×
1x.note: before the epic there was no presentation stage: cars were extrapolated ahead of the newest frame in the vertex shader, so the picture did not trail it (it could run ahead and step back: i4)

20x.source: epic_probe.mjs: the Diagnostics presentation lag, median of 100 ms samples over 10 s at 20×
20x.note: before the epic there was no presentation stage: cars were extrapolated ahead of the newest frame in the vertex shader, so the picture did not trail it (it could run ahead and step back: i4)

hardware.renderer: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Pro, Unspecified Version)
hardware.how: headed Chromium on the GPU (no SwiftShader flags), epic_probe.mjs with "headed", dev server per build; display refresh 120 Hz

conditions.note: shared machine; the 1-minute load average was 7–22 at the starts of the SwiftShader runs and 10–20 for the hardware runs (other sessions). This run set replaces an earlier one (Gold r1 MAJOR 1: its probe missed the vehicle ArrayBuffer)
